title: [SDK 50] Pod install error: The Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends upon `glog`, which does not define modules.
body: I have an SDK 50 project with a minimal reproducible example at https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/tree/0.73.0. The GitHub Actions build fails during pod installation with: `[!] The following Swift pods cannot yet be integrated as static libraries: The Swift pod ExpoModulesCore depends upon glog, which does not define modules.` The failing action is https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/actions/runs/7194009870/job/19593603408. Environment details are in the action log.

symptoms_visible: My GitHub Actions build exits with code 1 during pod installation because CocoaPods says the Swift pod ExpoModulesCore depends on glog, which does not define modules.
N0.label: N0 CI pod installation error reported

symptoms_visible: The workflow still reaches the ExpoModulesCore and glog module error during pod installation.
N1.label: N1 direct dependency ruled out

symptoms_visible: There is no expo-modules-core entry in my package.json for me to remove, and the original workflow still has the pod installation error.
N1_x.label: N1_x dependency-removal suggestion rejected

symptoms_visible: The v0.73.0-5 workflow run fails during pod installation, while the v0.73.0-6 run succeeds when tested with runs-on set to macos-13; that runner setting is the only change in the diff.
N2.label: N2 runner comparison isolates environment

symptoms_visible: After keeping the workflow on macos-13, pod installation succeeds and the ExpoModulesCore-to-glog module error no longer occurs in my GitHub Actions build.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on newer macOS runner

question_patterns: Is expo-modules-core listed directly in your package.json dependencies?
Can you confirm whether ExpoModulesCore is installed directly or only arrives transitively through expo?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I don't have expo-modules-core in my dependencies.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, expo-modules-core is explicitly listed in my package.json at a version that does not match my Expo SDK.
My package.json uses alphabetical ordering for dependencies.

edges.comment: Reporter c1: the original reporter explicitly states that expo-modules-core is not a direct dependency. This edge describes only the opening reporter's project, not the later participants' deployments.

solution.intent: Remove expo-modules-core from package.json, reinstall JavaScript dependencies, and reinstall the pods so Expo can select it transitively.
solution.concrete_example: Delete expo-modules-core from package.json, run yarn again, and reinstall the pods.

edges.comment: Participant1 c0 suggested and preemptively closed on this theory. Reporter c1 rejected it with project-specific evidence: expo-modules-core was not listed directly, so there was no such dependency to remove.

question_patterns: Can you run the workflow on another macOS runner and share both run logs and the workflow diff?
Please test the same workflow on macos-13 and tell me the result and whether anything else changed between the runs.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The pod install fails in tag v0.73.0-5 and succeeds in tag v0.73.0-6. I shared both action logs and the comparison diff; the only change is changing the runner to `runs-on: macos-13`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same ExpoModulesCore and glog error occurs on both runners with an otherwise identical workflow.
The macos-13 run succeeds, but the comparison also contains an unrelated documentation edit.

edges.comment: Reporter c1 and c15: the original reporter tested macos-13, supplied the failing and successful action logs, and confirmed that the runner selection was the only functional diff. This is raw comparison output; attributing it to the runner's Xcode/toolchain is engineer-side inference.

question_patterns: Since expo-modules-core is not direct, can you test the unchanged project on macos-13 and share the outcome?
Can you share the failing and successful workflow logs and state what changed between them?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The v0.73.0-5 pod install log fails, and the v0.73.0-6 log succeeds. The comparison shows that the only change is `runs-on: macos-13`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Switching to macos-13 produces exactly the same glog module error.
The successful comparison uses macos-13 and also changes only a comment in the workflow file.

edges.comment: Recovery from the rejected c0 dependency theory using the reporter's c1/c15 runner comparison. No setup or symptom from another participant is merged into the reporter's causal chain.

solution.intent: Use a newer macOS CI runner with a newer compatible Xcode toolchain instead of treating expo-modules-core as an invalid direct dependency, and retain the change only after the same workflow completes pod installation successfully.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the GitHub Actions job on `runs-on: macos-13`, rerun the unchanged pod installation, and confirm that the ExpoModulesCore/glog module error is gone before considering the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established only that changing the runner to macos-13 was the sole workflow change and made pod installation succeed. Mapping the runner difference to the older versus newer Xcode/toolchain behavior is the maintainer's interpretation from c17 and the surrounding reports, not a conclusion supplied by the reporter.

edges.comment: Resolution for the opening reporter comes from c1 and c15: the workflow succeeds after its only functional change is runs-on: macos-13. Participant1 c17 interprets this as an old-Xcode/toolchain issue. Later comments describe separate projects and alternative problems, so they are not chained onto this reporter's resolution.

solution.intent: Test and adopt a newer macOS GitHub Actions runner so pod installation uses a newer compatible Apple toolchain, then verify the result with an otherwise unchanged workflow.
solution.concrete_example: Change the job to `runs-on: macos-13`, rerun it without changing the project dependencies, and keep the runner change if pod install completes without the ExpoModulesCore/glog error.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut permits the ultimately successful runner/toolchain test as the first proposal. The reporter must still execute the comparison and report success before resolution; the shortcut does not assume that result in advance.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the thread's first handler move was the falsified direct-dependency removal. It represents proposing the reporter's actual successful macos-13 comparison immediately, while skipping the later dependency clarification and comparison evidence.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause for the opening reporter as an older macOS CI/Xcode toolchain compatibility problem exposed while integrating ExpoModulesCore with glog, grounded in the otherwise-identical runner comparison rather than inferred from the CocoaPods text alone.
Must recommend using macos-13 or an equivalently newer compatible CI toolchain and rerunning the same pod installation.
Must not treat removal of a direct expo-modules-core dependency as the fix for this reporter, because the reporter confirmed that no such direct dependency exists.

Must not substitute unrelated later-thread remedies from other projects, such as global modular headers, patching podspecs, changing Expo major versions, or cleaning pods, for the reporter's demonstrated runner-based resolution.
Must require a successful pod-install run on the changed runner before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable open-source maintainer using GitHub Actions for a React Native and Expo integration; comfortable sharing action logs, tags, repository diffs, and changing CI runner configuration.
persona_hint.communication_style: Very concise and evidence-oriented; responds with direct corrections, links to failing and successful runs, and emphasizes the exact one-line workflow difference.
